title: Measuring a phrase with EB Garamond before layout

steps.title: The ruler spans the phrase’s advance
steps.line: The ruler ends after the final glyph’s advance.
steps.caption: “Ink on paper” advances 5.88 scene units in EB Garamond, including the spaces between its words. A following word would add another space, which this ruler does not include. This scene explicitly requests EB Garamond; pen-and-ink supplies the paper and colours.
steps.picture: A dimension line marked “5.88 units”; 1 label.

steps.title: The same phrase advances differently in each cut
steps.line: Regular, Bold and Italic keep the text and size fixed.
steps.caption: The first ruler measured text at 1.2 units; these three rows use 0.9. At that shared size, “Ink on paper” advances 4.41 units in Regular, 4.85 in Bold and 4.24 in Italic. Each EB Garamond cut supplies its own captured paths, so the page needs no font download.
steps.picture: The same words in three EB Garamond cuts: Regular, advance 4.41; Bold, advance 4.85; Italic, advance 4.24. Each cut was requested and captured from its own source font.

steps.title: The diagram measures labels before placing nodes
steps.line: Ink and Paper keep EB Garamond’s measured proportions.
steps.caption: The arrow connects Ink and Paper, both drawn in the requested EB Garamond face. Natural lettering captures their advances, so the renderer places the boxes without stretching either label to a preset width.
